definition: K-means clustering partitions observations into a chosen number of groups by iteratively updating cluster centroids and assigning observations to nearby centroids.
example: A retailer groups stores by similar traffic and transaction patterns after scaling the features.

definition: Kahoot! is a learning platform for running interactive quizzes and activities on participants' devices.
example: A teacher runs a live review quiz and discusses the questions many students missed.

definition: KairosDB is a database system for ingesting and querying time-series measurements.
example: An operations team queries hourly aggregates of sensor readings.

definition: Katalon Studio is an integrated tool for creating and running automated application tests.
example: A tester records a web checkout flow and checks the resulting confirmation page.

definition: Kenna Security refers to a vulnerability-management platform that prioritizes remediation using risk signals and asset information.
example: A security team ranks known vulnerabilities on its inventory to decide which fixes to deploy first.

definition: Keras is a high-level Python API for defining, training and using neural networks.
example: A developer builds a classifier as a sequence of layers and trains it on labeled images.

definition: Kinesitherapy uses therapeutic movement and exercise to restore or improve physical function.
example: A rehabilitation clinician guides a patient through a prescribed range-of-motion exercise.

definition: Kinetic typography designs moving text to communicate timing, emphasis or meaning.
example: A title designer animates words in sync with the narrator's emphasis.

definition: Knockout.js is a JavaScript library that binds interface elements to observable data in a view model.
example: A shopping page updates the price total when a user changes an item count.

definition: Know Your Third Party is a third-party risk management platform for exchanging and evaluating due-diligence information.
example: A compliance team collects supplier assessment responses in a shared workflow.
sense_note: The abbreviation may also refer to a generic due-diligence practice.

definition: KPI reporting measures and communicates key indicators tied to organizational goals.
example: A manager reports the weekly on-time shipment rate against its target.

definition: The Kyoto Protocol is an international climate treaty that set binding greenhouse-gas reduction or limitation commitments for specified parties.
example: A national emissions inventory supports reporting against an applicable commitment.

definition: Kyriba is treasury management software for tasks such as cash visibility, payments, liquidity planning and financial risk management.
example: A treasury analyst consolidates balances from several banks to review the day's cash position.

definition: A label edge router is a router at a Multiprotocol Label Switching domain boundary that adds, removes or processes packet labels.
example: An ingress router classifies incoming traffic and applies a label for its forwarding path.

definition: A label printer produces labels carrying text, barcodes or graphics on compatible stock.
example: A warehouse worker prints barcode labels for outgoing cartons.

definition: LabVIEW is a graphical programming environment for building measurement, automation and instrument-control applications.
example: A technician builds a program to acquire measurements and plot them live.

definition: Landing page optimization improves a destination web page to help visitors complete a defined action.
example: An analyst tests whether a clearer signup form raises its completion rate.

definition: Lando is a tool for configuring and running local development environments using containers.
example: A developer starts a reproducible web server and database using a project's Lando configuration.

definition: Landscape painting depicts natural or built outdoor scenery using painted color, composition and perspective.
example: An artist paints a valley and uses softer colors to suggest distant hills.

definition: Landscaping and yard care involve designing, installing or maintaining outdoor grounds and plantings.
example: A grounds crew prunes shrubs and repairs a stretch of turf.

definition: LangChain is a software framework for assembling language-model applications with components such as prompts, retrieval and tool calls.
example: A developer combines document retrieval and a language model to answer handbook questions.

definition: Language interpretation and translation convey meaning between languages, generally with interpreting for spoken or signed messages and translation for written material.
example: An interpreter relays a meeting discussion while a translator prepares its written summary in another language.

definition: Language teaching develops learners' comprehension and expression in a language through instruction and practice.
example: A teacher uses role-play to help beginners practice asking for directions.

definition: A laser level projects a beam or line to establish reference points for level, plumb or alignment work.
example: An installer uses a horizontal beam to align wall-mounted cabinets.

definition: LDRA Testbed is a software analysis and testing tool for assessing code quality, coding-standard compliance and test coverage.
example: A quality engineer checks embedded software for violations of a project's coding rules.

definition: Lean principles guide work improvement by defining customer value, reducing waste and improving how value-producing activities flow.
example: A production team reduces the time parts wait between inspection and assembly.

definition: Learner analysis examines learners' prior knowledge, goals, needs and constraints to guide instructional decisions.
example: A course designer surveys employees' experience before selecting prerequisite exercises.

definition: Learner experience design shapes activities, materials and interactions around how people engage with and learn from them.
example: A designer pairs a realistic task with immediate feedback and a guided retry.

definition: Learning agility is the ability to learn from experience and apply that learning in unfamiliar situations.
example: After trialing a new tool, a team member applies what worked to a different project.

definition: LEGO Digital Designer was a software tool for building virtual models from digital LEGO elements.
example: A builder tries different brick arrangements before assembling a physical model.

definition: Less.js is a JavaScript implementation of a preprocessor that compiles Less syntax, such as variables and mixins, into CSS.
example: A developer defines a reusable color variable and compiles the stylesheet for a website.

definition: Levelator is an audio processing tool that evens out variations in recorded speech levels.
example: A podcast editor uses it to balance a quiet presenter and a louder guest.

definition: LIBSVM is a library for support vector machine classification, regression and related modeling tasks.
example: An analyst trains a support vector classifier to distinguish two categories of text.

definition: LiDAR measures distances by emitting laser light and analyzing the returned signal, often to create three-dimensional point data.
example: A survey crew maps terrain and structures along a road.

definition: Life skills are practical abilities for managing daily responsibilities, relationships and decisions.
example: A learner makes a budget and schedules bill payments.

definition: Lightcast provides labor-market data and analytics about jobs, occupations and skills.
example: An analyst uses job-posting data to identify frequently requested qualifications.

definition: LightGBM is a library for training gradient-boosted decision tree models for classification, regression and ranking.
example: An analyst trains a model to predict customer churn from account data.

definition: Lighting design plans the placement, intensity, color and direction of light to support function or visual intent.
example: A designer sets light positions and levels to keep actors visible while creating a nighttime mood.
sense_note: The label spans stage, architectural and other lighting contexts.

definition: LightTools is optical design and simulation software for modeling illumination systems and light propagation.
example: An optical engineer simulates how evenly a light guide illuminates a display.

definition: The LinkedIn API provides programmatic access to authorized LinkedIn features or data under applicable permissions.
example: An application with approved access publishes content to a managed organization page.
